```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`sharedimp` implements the linear-regression variant of ultra-marginal
feature importance (UMFI-LR; Janssen, Guan and Robeva, AISTATS 2023) in a
form that fits modern resampling-based workflows. The package does not
introduce a new importance measure. It makes an existing one safe to use:
the residualization step is estimated inside each training fold, the two
models being compared are evaluated on the same assessment rows, the sign of
the result does not depend on the metric, and negative values are not hidden.

## The idea in one paragraph

Take an *anchor* feature $X_i$. Regress every other feature $X_j$ on $X_i$
(ordinary least squares with an intercept) and keep the residuals
$R_j = X_j - a_j - b_j X_i$. By construction the residuals are uncorrelated
with the anchor on the data used to fit them. Now compare two models of $y$:

* **full**: $[X_i, R_{-i}]$ — the anchor plus the residualized others;
* **reduced**: $[R_{-i}]$ — the residualized others only.

The out-of-sample gain of the full model over the reduced model is the
importance of $X_i$. Because the linear part of $X_i$ has been removed from
the other features, information that $X_i$ *shares* with correlated
features is credited to $X_i$ rather than being split or lost, which is what
distinguishes UMFI from ablation and permutation importance for correlated
predictors.

## A worked example

```{r setup}
library(sharedimp)
set.seed(2026)
n <- 300
x <- data.frame(
  x1 = rnorm(n),
  x2 = rnorm(n),
  x3 = rnorm(n),
  x4 = rnorm(n)
)
x$x5 <- x$x1 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.2) # a noisy copy of x1
y <- 3 * x$x1 + 2 * x$x2 + 1 * x$x3 + rnorm(n)
```

`x4` is pure noise and `x5` is a near-duplicate of `x1`. With the fast,
deterministic linear learner and the mean squared error:

```{r linear}
res <- shared_importance(x, y, learner = "linear", v = 5, seed = 1)
res
```

Importance is `-(MSE_full - MSE_reduced)`, i.e. the increase in MSE caused by
dropping the anchor while keeping the residualized others. For an
independent linear-Gaussian design it is approximately $\beta_i^2
\mathrm{Var}(X_i)$: roughly 9, 4 and 1 for `x1`, `x2`, `x3`, and 0 for the
noise feature. The near-duplicate `x5` receives almost the same importance as
`x1`: once `x1` is residualized on `x5`, little of `x1` is left, so `x5`
carries the shared signal. This is the duplication-symmetry property of UMFI.

The per-fold paired metrics are always kept:

```{r folds}
fold_results(res)
```

Negative fold values for `x4` are expected and are reported as they are.

## Choosing the learner and the metric

The default learner is a random forest (`ranger`, 500 trees, `min_n = 5`)
with fixed hyperparameters. Any `parsnip` model specification can be used
instead, as can a pair of `fit`/`predict` functions wrapped with
`sharedimp_learner()`.

```{r rf, eval = requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)}
res_rf <- shared_importance(x, y, v = 5, seed = 1)
res_rf$importance
```

Metrics come from `yardstick`. Scores are always reported oriented so that
greater is better: the metric itself for a metric to maximize (`"r2"`,
`"accuracy"`, `"roc_auc"`) and its negative for a metric to minimize
(`"mse"`, `"rmse"`, `"mae"`, `"log_loss"`). Importance is
`score_full - score_reduced` in both cases, so it is positive whenever the
anchor helps. (`"r2"` is `1 - SS_res / SS_tot`, the scikit-learn `r2`;
yardstick's squared-correlation `"rsq"` is also available but is a different
quantity.)

```{r r2}
shared_importance(x, y, learner = "linear", metric = "r2", v = 5, seed = 1)$importance
```

## Classification

For a factor response the task is classification. The first factor level is
the event level for probability metrics, and folds are stratified by `y`.

```{r classification}
yb <- factor(ifelse(y > median(y), "high", "low"), levels = c("high", "low"))
res_b <- shared_importance(x, yb, learner = "linear", metric = "log_loss", v = 5, seed = 1)
res_b$importance
```

Multiclass responses work the same way; `"roc_auc"` then uses the Hand-Till
estimator and `"log_loss"` the multinomial log loss.

## Reproducibility and explicit folds

`seed` controls fold generation and any stochastic learner under a local RNG
state, leaving the caller's random stream untouched. For comparisons across
software (for example with the Python implementation of the same
specification) pass explicit folds, either an `rsample` `rset` or a vector of
fold labels:

```{r folds-explicit}
labels <- rep(1:5, length.out = n)
res_fixed <- shared_importance(x, y, learner = "linear", resamples = labels)
res_fixed$resampling
```

## What the numbers are and are not

The values are out-of-sample predictive gains for a given learner, metric
and resampling scheme. They are not causal effects, not conditional effects,
and not regression coefficients. The `importance_std` column is the
dispersion of the split-level values and is purely descriptive; the package
deliberately provides no confidence intervals or p-values.

The output tables use the column names shared with the Python package
(`feature`, `importance`, `importance_std`, `score_full`, `score_reduced`,
`n_splits`; per split additionally `split`, `n_train`, `n_test`). With a
deterministic learner and explicit splits the two packages produce the same
numbers.

## Relation to the reference UMFI implementation

The reference implementation (<https://github.com/HydroML/UMFI>) fits the
residualization on the whole data set, gates it on a slope p-value, scores
random forests by out-of-bag $R^2$ or accuracy with floors, and sets negative
values to zero. `sharedimp` residualizes inside each training fold, always
residualizes, uses paired per-fold assessment metrics with any learner, and
keeps negative values. Numerical identity is therefore not expected; the
specification and a recorded comparison are in the `docs/` directory of the
source repository.
